name: fill_rows_with_pattern
description: Loops eleven times, storing a repeated 32-bit constant at a pointer-derived location and advancing by a fixed row stride on each pass. Five helper routines are called on every pass.

name: retry_poll_and_store_result
description: Calls helper routines in a loop of up to ten tries, returning an error code if the wait expires or the second helper's result is wrong. When the checks pass it stores a decremented value and a constant into the frame and returns zero.

name: scan_slots_for_matching_word
description: Walks up to eleven table slots, polling a status byte between checks and comparing a stored word with a target value. It returns zero when the walk ends or the status says stop, a minus-one code on an abort, and other error codes on mismatches or missing data.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return instruction with no memory, register or routine references, so calling it does nothing.

name: set_flag_bit_and_count
description: Sets one bit in a 16-bit flag word, with the bit number taken from the low five bits of register D3, and then increments the 16-bit counter located just before the same base pointer.

name: clear_ten_table_entries
description: Writes zero to a longword at the start of each of ten table entries, moving the pointer forward by a fixed entry size on each pass.

name: rearrange_long_into_halves
description: Calls a helper to obtain a 32-bit value and returns it rearranged so the low word becomes the high word and the top byte becomes the low word.

name: interleave_longword_even_bits
description: Reads two adjacent longwords from the pointer in A0 and merges their even-numbered bits: bits from the second longword stay in even positions and bits from the first move to odd positions.

name: forward_helper_result_onward
description: Calls a helper to obtain a 32-bit value and passes that value unchanged to a second routine, returning nothing.

name: compute_masked_xor_checksum
description: XORs ten consecutive longwords that start eight bytes past the base pointer and keeps only the even-numbered bits of the result.

name: compute_counted_xor_checksum
description: XORs a run of longwords starting at the A0 pointer and keeps only the even-numbered bits of the result. The run length comes from register D1, treated as a byte count and divided by four.

name: fill_block_with_alternating_pattern
description: Fills a memory block with a repeated alternating-bit longword pattern, writing backwards from the end. The block length depends on a flag byte in the frame: one length for a flag of one, a much longer one otherwise.

name: interleave_two_longword_streams
description: Reads 128 longwords from the A0 pointer and 128 more from the block that follows them, merging each pair's even-numbered bits into the destination array.

name: clear_flags_and_mix_words
description: Loops over a count derived from the first argument's byte count divided by four, calling a flag-clearing helper and a word-mixing helper on each pass. It then calls both helpers once more and returns both arguments.

name: mix_and_update_status_byte
description: Calls two helper routines and then updates a status byte through the pointer: if the preceding byte's low bit is clear it sets the top bit, leaving the byte unchanged when bit six is already set; otherwise it clears the top bit and writes the byte back.

name: update_status_byte_flags
description: Reads a status byte through the pointer and updates it using bit zero of the preceding byte, with no helper calls. When that bit is clear it sets the top bit unless bit six is already set; when the bit is set it clears the top bit.

name: start_disk_dma_read
description: Prepares a floppy-disk DMA read: it enables disk DMA in the control registers, loads the disk pointer from the argument, writes the disk sync word, and starts the transfer with a length derived from the argument word.

name: check_disk_status_then_reset
description: Tests a status bit once through the pointer; if it is set, the routine writes two disk and interrupt control values and returns zero. If it is clear, it calls a helper, writes the same two values, and returns minus one.

name: write_audio_disk_control_word
description: Writes a fixed control word to the audio and disk control register and, when a frame flag is negative, also writes an all-ones byte to a second register after computing a bit index from a frame value.

name: set_cia_port_bit
description: Computes a bit index from a frame value plus three, masked to five bits, then sets that bit in the byte passed in register D1 and writes the result to the CIA port B register.

name: poll_ciab_port_until_one
description: Writes an all-ones value to the CIA port B register, then repeatedly calls a helper and waits while bit zero of the port register stays set, looping until the helper returns one. It returns zero.

name: update_table_entry_with_steps
description: Reads a word from a global table at an index taken from the frame and, if the entry is negative, calls a helper and may return that result early. It then calls a helper as many times as the difference between the new and stored values, stores the new word in the table and returns zero.

name: poll_input_bit_then_clear
description: Polls bit four of a global port value up to 86 times, calling a helper between polls. When the bit clears it zeroes a word in a table selected by a frame index and returns zero; if the bit never clears it returns a timeout code.

name: drive_ciab_port_and_wait
description: Takes a value from a helper and clears its second bit when the register argument is non-negative, then writes it to the CIA port B register with bit zero set. It then calls a helper and waits while bit zero stays set, repeating until the helper returns one, and returns zero.

name: write_helper_result_to_port
description: Calls a helper and writes its result to the CIA port B register.

name: compute_port_mask_byte
description: Builds a byte from a port register value with its lower seven bits forced on and the bit chosen by a frame index plus three cleared. It also clears bit two when the matching table entry has its low bit set, and returns that byte together with the second argument.

name: poll_helper_until_result_one
description: Repeatedly calls a helper, waiting between calls while bit zero of a global port value stays set, and returns zero once the helper returns one.

name: program_ciab_timer_when_clear
description: When bit zero of a global port value is clear and the argument is not one, writes three control values to the CIA timer registers. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: load_fixed_ciab_timer_values
description: Writes three fixed values in sequence to the CIA timer control and timer high and low registers.

name: enable_dma_and_interrupts
description: Stores a constant, calls a helper, then writes two enable values to the DMA and interrupt control registers before calling a fixed-address routine. The decompiled listing ends at an unimplemented instruction, so the rest of the routine is not recoverable from this evidence.

name: invoke_jump_vector_and_helpers
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are known: a 65-instruction routine that calls one jump-table entry and six other routines. Its purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: repeat_helper_thirty_two_times
description: Calls a fixed-address routine three times, then calls a helper routine thirty-two times in a counted loop.

name: step_nibbles_toward_target
description: Compares three 4-bit fields of one word with the matching fields of another and moves each differing field one step toward its target. Fields that already match are left unchanged.

name: write_control_value_sequence
description: Calls a fixed-address routine, then writes a fixed run of twenty values in order to a single global location. The values are mostly the same few constants, with a few different ones.

name: build_two_address_tables
description: Calls a fixed-address routine, programs three control values, and fills two tables of four entries each with 32-bit addresses split into high and low words, stepping by the current value of a global location between entries. It then writes table addresses and control values to the registers.

name: build_one_address_table
description: Calls a fixed-address routine, programs three control values, and fills one table of four entries with 32-bit addresses split into high and low words, stepping by the current value of a global location. It then writes two control values.

name: build_six_address_table
description: Calls a fixed-address routine, programs three control values, and fills one table of six entries with 32-bit addresses split into high and low words, stepping by the current value of a global location. It then writes two control values.

name: wait_for_raster_line_change
description: Spins until a masked value read from the video position register reaches a specific value, then spins until it moves off that value, and returns its first argument unchanged.

name: acknowledge_flag_and_count
description: Writes the first flag bit of a global word back as an acknowledgement when it is set. When the second bit is set it calls a helper and increments a counter, otherwise it returns with no change.

name: return_empty_sprite_stub
description: The decompiled body is only a return, so it does nothing in the code shown, even though the listing metadata says sprite pointer and interrupt registers are referenced.

name: set_top_bit_after_helpers
description: Calls two helper routines, then sets the top bit of a global byte. The two conditional writes always leave that bit set.

name: pack_word_flags_into_byte
description: Clears a byte through the second pointer, then sets its low four bits from specific bits of the word at the first pointer. Two bits come from the word exclusive-ORed with itself shifted right by one, and two come directly from other word bits.

name: send_serial_byte_when_flagged
description: When bit four of a global byte is clear and bit three is set, it runs a keyboard serial transfer: a rotated complement of the byte is looked up in a fixed table, written out, and the routine waits for bit zero to set. Otherwise it only resets the byte to eight, and in both cases it returns its argument.

name: send_keyboard_serial_byte
description: Takes a rotated complement of a global byte, looks it up in a fixed byte table and writes the result to the keyboard serial register. It then waits until bit zero of the global is set before writing its closing control values.

name: verify_form_tag_and_scan
description: Checks that the first longword at the pointer holds the tag FORM and returns one if it does not. Otherwise it calls three helpers, then repeats nested scans, advancing the pointer by a global value on each outer pass, and returns zero once a helper returns zero.

name: locate_bmhd_chunk_value
description: Advances a pointer two bytes at a time until it reaches the four-character tag BMHD, then returns a word stored ten bytes after that tag, minus one.

name: seek_to_body_chunk
description: Advances a pointer two bytes at a time until it reaches the four-character tag BODY, leaving the pointer at that tag and changing no memory.

name: pack_cmap_colors_to_nibbles
description: Searches forward for the tag CMAP, then converts each three-byte color entry in its data into two bytes holding the high four bits of each channel. The converted bytes are written to a fixed buffer.

name: unpack_packbits_stream
description: Decompresses PackBits-style run-length data: a non-negative control byte copies the following bytes literally, a negative one repeats the next byte, and the value 128 is skipped. It stops once the expected output count is reached.

name: stub_undecoded_single_instruction
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are known: a one-instruction routine, reached from outside static flow, that calls nothing. Its purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: The routine is a single return with no other instructions, so it does nothing when executed.

name: setup_tables_then_loop_forever
description: Makes four calls through a base-pointer jump table, stores a routine address in a global slot and writes constants into four table pairs. It then calls more routines, with two extra calls only on one result, and always ends in an endless loop.

name: rotate_keyboard_serial_byte
description: When bit three of a global byte is set, it rotates the complemented byte, clears bit three, and returns the byte within its return value. Otherwise it sets the byte to eight and returns its argument unchanged; the keyboard serial register is referenced.

name: set_flag_bit_around_helper
description: Sets bit six of a global control byte, calls a helper, clears that bit again, then writes the value eight to the same byte and returns its argument.

name: call_two_indirect_handlers
description: Loads a function pointer from a global slot and calls it through a method at a fixed offset of another object, then makes an indirect call through a second pointer. The second target could not be recovered from the decompiled jump table.

name: copy_pointer_after_noop_call
description: Calls a routine that returns immediately, then copies a pointer from one global slot into another.

name: check_tag_match_flag
description: Compares the four-character tag CR2B at the A4 pointer with the longword there, stores one or zero in a global flag, then calls a helper.

name: spin_forever_without_return
description: Enters an endless loop with no body and never returns to the caller. The listing metadata mentions a video position register, but the decoded body shows no access to it.

name: call_handler_when_enabled
description: When the byte argument is zero and the word argument is nonzero, calls a handler through a pointer at a fixed offset of a global object. It returns the long argument unchanged in either case.

name: enter_boot_block_unanalysed
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are known: a three-instruction boot block entry that calls one routine. Its purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: stub_undecoded_six_instructions
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are known: a six-instruction routine whose address is taken PC-relatively and that is called by one routine. Its purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: init_tables_then_loop_forever
description: Writes a series of addresses to a global slot, sets four pairs of table words, and calls routines between these steps. It then makes two extra calls on one result and ends in an endless loop; the listing also records color and video position registers as touched.

name: install_interrupt_handler_entry
description: Writes two enable values to the DMA and interrupt control registers, stores a routine address and the address of a global slot in global slots, and writes a further control value.

name: acknowledge_interrupt_request
description: Writes bit four alone to the interrupt request register and returns its arguments unchanged.

name: convert_position_to_track_sector
description: Rejects a position above a fixed limit, otherwise divides it by eleven to get a track and a sector remainder, with a flag-dependent adjustment. It then loops over the sectors left, calling helpers for each chunk, and returns the final status along with a decoded position value.

name: read_sector_with_retries
description: Tries up to three times to read a disk sector, clearing three frame words on each attempt. When the disk status bit is set, it stores a fill pattern and the disk sync word in the buffer, calls helpers, compares two frame words, and returns zero on success or an error code otherwise.

name: run_disk_dma_retry_loop
description: Repeats up to three times while a disk status bit is set, writing audio and disk control values, setting the disk pointer from a frame value and writing control and sync values before calling helpers. It returns an error code when the status bit is clear, otherwise the last helper result.

name: write_sync_pattern_rows
description: Loops eleven times, storing a repeated pair of disk sync words at a pointer-derived location and advancing by a fixed stride each pass. Five helper routines are called on every pass.

name: retry_poll_and_store_result
description: Calls helper routines in a loop of up to ten tries, returning an error code if the wait expires or the second helper's result is wrong. When the checks pass it stores a decremented value and a constant into the frame and returns zero.

name: program_ciab_timer_when_clear

name: load_fixed_ciab_timer_values
description: Writes three fixed values in sequence to the CIA timer control and timer high and low registers.

name: copy_masked_color_value
description: If bit zero of a byte in a record reached through a pointer stored in a global slot is set, it copies a word from that record, substitutes eight for zero, masks off the low three bits and substitutes eight again if that gives zero. Otherwise the routine loops forever.

name: relocate_image_and_launch
description: Walks a relocation table, adding the buffer's base address to each listed longword, then copies the adjusted image into a fixed low-memory address in longword steps and calls into it.

name: advance_word_with_wrap
description: Adds an offset to the longword at the pointer; when the result reaches a limit held in another register, it is re-based to the fixed low base address plus the excess over that limit.

name: unpack_rnc_stream
description: Checks for the RNC compressed-file signature and, if present, reads the sizes that follow and decodes the bit-packed data. The decoder copies literal runs and back-references from its own output, using helper routines to read bits and counts.

name: decode_matching_table_entry
description: Searches a table of word pairs for the first entry whose masked value matches a register value, then reads a byte count from that entry. When the count is above one it builds a bit-field value from the register and sets one further bit, and it may call a helper to adjust the field before returning it.

name: mask_word_or_call_helper
description: Masks a word from one register with a second word, and when a byte argument is below another byte argument it calls a helper and returns that result instead.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing when called.

name: read_four_bytes_into_register
description: Loops four times over consecutive bytes from the pointer, writing each one into the low byte of the result register, and returns that register.

name: build_canonical_code_table
description: Reads a count of symbols and their code lengths from the input, then assigns canonical codes by walking lengths from one to sixteen, reversing the bit order of each code and storing masks, values and lengths in a table. The routine returns nothing.

name: call_indirect_handler_pair
description: Calls a method at a fixed offset of an object reached through a global slot, then makes an indirect call through a second pointer that could not be recovered from the jump table.

name: run_endless_update_loop
description: Initialises several variables, waits for the blitter to become idle before programming its registers, then loops forever. Each pass calls several routines, maps a status word to a value of three, five or eight, and clears a set of global slots.

name: initialise_record_fields
description: Clears a longword in a record reached through the A5 base, copies a global value into one word field, and stores the constant two into another word field.

name: initialise_tables_and_pointers
description: Zeroes three large longword tables and one further block, preserving several record fields around the clearing, then sets pointer slots. It fills three word tables with multiples of their index: 512 entries scaled by a stride of 96 stored in the record, and two 256-entry tables scaled by 192 and 120.

name: fill_tables_and_program_blitter
description: Writes a long list of constants to a global location, then programs blitter registers in four passes, each after waiting for the blitter to be idle. It then fills several word tables with values from a helper routine, scaled by factors of eight and two.

name: write_three_value_pairs
description: Writes three values to a global location in sequence, each followed by the constant three.

name: wait_for_tag_then_verify
description: Repeatedly calls a helper until the first longword of a fixed block equals the four-character tag CR2A, then calls a verification helper and retries it up to six times. If every attempt succeeds it returns the final value, and if the verification fails it loops forever writing a helper result to a global location.

name: mask_word_or_call_helper

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return with no instructions that modify memory or registers, so it does nothing when called.

name: read_four_bytes_into_register
description: Loops four times over consecutive bytes from the pointer, writing each one into the low byte of the result register, and returns that register.

name: build_canonical_code_table
description: Reads a count of symbols and their code lengths from the input, then assigns canonical codes by walking lengths from one to sixteen, reversing the bit order of each code and storing masks, values and lengths in a table. The routine returns nothing.

name: advance_seed_and_scale
description: Advances a 32-bit seed stored in a record with a shift-and-XOR feedback step, repeated for each bit of the argument. It then returns the low word of the seed when the argument is zero, or otherwise the high word of the seed's low half multiplied by the argument.

name: multiply_high_words
description: Multiplies the low words of two register values and returns the upper 16 bits of the 32-bit product.

name: setup_interrupt_vector_slots
description: Writes six control values in sequence, including interrupt and DMA enable values, and stores a routine address in two global slots. The routine returns nothing.

name: acknowledge_after_helper_call
description: Calls a helper, writes bit four alone to the interrupt request register, and returns its arguments unchanged.

name: count_interrupt_and_acknowledge
description: Calls two routines, increments a 16-bit counter stored at a fixed address, then writes bit four alone to the interrupt request register and returns its arguments.

name: initialise_audio_dma_tables
description: Clears a block of 52 longwords, builds a table of running offsets from a source table, and stores a handler address in thirteen entries. It finishes by writing values to the audio volume, DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: clear_audio_volumes_and_reset
description: Zeroes the four audio channel volume registers, clears one bit of a global control value, writes a few control constants, and copies a saved value back into a global slot.

name: step_music_channels_tick
description: When the tick counter is still running, this updates four audio channel records, applying slide and effect commands from a switch and writing the results to the channel registers. Otherwise it reads the next packed event for each channel from a stream; the bundled listing is cut off mid-routine, so the rest is not recoverable.

name: call_unrecovered_jump_target
description: Makes an indirect call through a pointer the decompiler could not recover from its jump table, then returns.

name: decode_bitstream_commands
description: Runs a shared decoder loop that shifts a control word, reads literal bytes or copy commands from the input, and writes the results through several pointer slots. It leaves through an indirect call when a command code is out of range, and the listing shows only this interior entry point.

name: decode_bitstream_commands
description: Stores the low byte of a register at a fixed flag location, then runs the same shared decoder loop.

name: decode_bitstream_commands
description: Writes a fixed flag byte into the frame, then runs the same shared decoder loop.

name: decode_bitstream_commands
description: Stores a register word in a fixed pointer slot, then runs the shared decoder loop that shifts control bits and reads literal or copy commands from the input.

name: decode_bitstream_commands
description: Merges the low byte of a register into a control value with bit one cleared, then runs the shared decoder loop.

name: slide_period_down_and_dispatch
description: Subtracts a slide amount from a channel's period, clamps it to a minimum and writes it to the channel's period register. It then walks the remaining channel records, calling an effect handler from a table for any nonzero command code up to eight.

name: slide_period_up_and_dispatch
description: Adds a slide amount to a channel's period, clamps it to a maximum and writes it to the channel's period register. It then walks the remaining channel records, calling an effect handler from a table for any nonzero command code up to eight.

name: lookup_value_and_dispatch
description: Looks up a value from a fixed table using an index derived from the channel's note and offset fields, or uses the channel's base value when the table entry is zero, then writes the result to the channel. It then walks the remaining channel records, calling an effect handler for any nonzero command code up to eight.

name: apply_volume_effect_and_dispatch
description: Scales a channel's volume from a fixed table and a stored nibble, adds a sign-adjusted offset, and writes the result to the channel register. When the command code is the volume-slide value it also adjusts and clamps the channel volume to sixty-four, then walks the remaining records calling effect handlers.

name: scale_volume_and_dispatch
description: Scales a channel's volume from a fixed table and a stored nibble, adds a sign-adjusted offset, and writes the result to the channel register. When the command code is the volume-slide value it also adjusts and clamps the channel volume to sixty-four, then walks the remaining records calling effect handlers.

name: set_period_difference_and_dispatch
description: Stores the difference between two register arguments as a channel period, updates a channel field, and applies the volume-slide step when the command code is the volume-slide value. It then walks the remaining channel records, calling effect handlers for nonzero command codes up to eight.

name: slide_volume_and_dispatch
description: Adds a sign-adjusted slide amount to a channel's volume, clamps it at sixty-four and writes it to the channel register, or uses a fixed fallback value when the result goes negative. It then walks the remaining channel records, calling effect handlers for nonzero command codes up to eight.

name: set_channel_fields_and_dispatch
description: Writes one fixed value into two channel fields, then walks the remaining channel records, calling an effect handler from a table for any nonzero command code up to eight.

name: slide_toward_target_and_dispatch
description: Moves a channel's value toward a stored target by a stored step, stopping at the target, and writes it to the channel register. When the command code is one specific value it also adds a sign-adjusted step to the volume and clamps it at sixty-four, then walks the remaining channel records calling effect handlers.

name: slide_toward_target_and_dispatch
description: Moves a channel's value toward a stored target by a stored step without updating the step field, stopping at the target, and writes it to the channel register. When the command code is one specific value it also adds a sign-adjusted step to the volume and clamps it at sixty-four, then walks the remaining channel records calling effect handlers.

name: slide_down_floor_and_dispatch
description: Subtracts a slide amount from a channel's value, stopping at a floor and setting the channel's target field to a fixed value when the floor is reached, and writes the value to the channel register. When the command code is one specific value it adds a sign-adjusted step to the volume, then walks the remaining records calling effect handlers.

name: store_handler_pointers_and_enable
description: Stores a constant, a routine address and a table address into global slots, then writes an enable value. The listing records interrupt and DMA control registers as touched.

name: load_audio_channel_pointers
description: Writes pointer and length pairs for the four audio channels from a table, preceded by an extra pair when a global flag is nonzero, then writes a further value and an enable. The listing records the audio channel pointer and length registers as touched.

name: call_fixed_routine_only
description: The decompiled body is only a call to a fixed-address routine, although the listing reports 234 instructions, so the rest of the routine is not visible here. Its purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: return_without_action
description: The routine is a single return with no other instructions, so it does nothing when executed.

name: return_without_action
description: The routine is a single return with no other instructions, so it does nothing when executed.

name: return_without_action
description: The routine is a single return with no other instructions, so it does nothing when executed.

name: return_without_action
description: The routine is a single return with no other instructions, so it does nothing when executed.

name: initialise_hardware_then_loop
description: Stores a context pointer, calls a helper through an object's method, and branches on the returned status to one of two configuration paths. It then clears a block of memory, writes clear-all masks to the audio and interrupt registers, and runs an endless loop that writes many custom chip register values and calls routines in sequence.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one routine and returns, doing nothing else.

name: call_routine_then_object_method
description: Calls one routine, then calls a method at a fixed offset of an object reached through a global slot, and returns the first routine's result.

name: call_object_method_and_return
description: Calls a method at a fixed offset of an object reached through a global slot and returns the incoming first argument unchanged.

name: run_hardware_setup_loop
description: Calls a method at a fixed offset of an object reached through a global slot, then runs an endless loop that writes many custom chip register values, clears a memory block and calls routines in sequence.

name: dispatch_status_then_hardware_loop
description: Calls a method at a fixed offset of an object and compares the returned status with two fixed codes. Unless it matches one of them, it jumps to a fallback routine; when it matches, it runs an endless loop that writes many custom chip register values, clears a memory block and calls routines in sequence.

name: call_routine_and_pass_through
description: Calls one routine and returns its two register arguments unchanged.

name: call_then_store_word_field
description: Calls one routine, stores the low word of the second argument into a field at offset ten of a record reached through the A3 base, and returns the first argument.

name: call_routine_and_pass_through
description: Calls one routine and returns its two register arguments unchanged.

name: add_loaded_value_with_carry
description: Calls one routine, then loads a longword through one of two pointers depending on whether the A3 value is negative. It returns that value summed with the first argument and the extended carry bit, with the second argument passed through.

name: add_pointer_value_with_carry
description: Loads a longword through the A3 pointer and returns it summed with a stack argument and the extended carry bit, passing the first argument through unchanged.

name: search_record_table_for_value
description: Chooses a global table as its start when a mode value is one or two, then scans it in six-byte steps for an entry equal to the argument. It stops at a negative entry or at a match.

name: search_word_table_for_value
description: Chooses a global table as its start when a mode value is one or two, then scans it in eight-byte steps for an entry equal to the argument. It stops at a negative entry or at a match.

name: process_string_by_mode
description: When the mode argument is zero, it matches the input string against a table of 16-byte entries, takes a 32-bit value from the matching entry and calls a helper repeatedly while reducing a counter by the helper's width. For mode two it calls a helper, and for mode five it records the input pointer and sets a flag when an argument equals the text 'ramp'; other modes return the argument unchanged.

name: call_object_method_passthrough
description: Calls a method at a fixed offset of an object reached through a global slot and returns its two register arguments unchanged.

name: call_routine_then_return
description: Calls one routine with a routine reference as its argument, then returns. The zero test on a register leads to the same return either way.

name: unpack_bitstream_with_copies
description: Decodes a packed bit stream into a buffer, alternating between back-reference copies and literal bytes chosen by control bits. It refills its bit reader as the stream is consumed and returns once the output pointer reaches the limit.

name: shift_bit_buffer_right
description: Shifts a 32-bit bit buffer right by the count argument, one bit at a time, loading the previous longword and setting its top bit as a sentinel whenever the buffer runs out.

name: return_without_action
description: The routine contains only a return, although the listing refers to the message 'Sorry, data are corrupted!'; the code shown does not display it.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The listing contains only undecodable bytes, so no behaviour can be recovered from this routine.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The listing contains only undecodable bytes, so no behaviour can be recovered from this routine.

name: clear_memory_and_run_loop
description: Writes clear-all masks to the audio and DMA registers, clears a large block of memory from a low address, and waits for a status value. It then runs an endless loop that writes many custom chip register values and calls routines in sequence.

name: dispatch_drive_command_with_polling
description: Dispatches on a small command code: most codes reset a set of status words and return the argument, while code three polls a status bit up to 400 times per attempt for up to six attempts, returning on the first match. It finishes by writing a masked value to the ADKCON control register unless it returned early.

name: set_flag_and_poll_status
description: Sets bit two of a global control value and clears a status word, then calls helpers up to four times while a second status word stays zero. It returns its two arguments unchanged.

name: poll_drive_for_matching_status
description: If the argument is non-negative, it stores the argument plus three in a control byte and calls two helpers. Otherwise it makes up to six attempts, clearing status bits and polling a status bit up to 400 times per attempt; it returns on a match, or writes a fixed failure value after the sixth attempt.

name: search_name_table_for_string
description: Compares a zero-terminated string with up to 192 fixed-length entries of sixteen bytes, comparing up to twelve characters in each. It returns as soon as an entry matches or the table is exhausted.

name: scan_buffer_for_position_match
description: Looks up a table entry from a nibble of the argument, then scans a large buffer for the low byte of that argument. On each match it computes a position in units of twelve, updates a control bit and the cached position when they change, and returns once a stop flag is set or the scan reaches its end.

name: compare_value_and_mark_error
description: Calls two helpers and, when the D7 argument equals the expected block size, compares the second helper result with an argument. A mismatch writes a fixed error code into a record field, and the routine returns the computed status with the second argument passed through.

name: delay_short_busy_loop
description: Spins through a fixed count of 512 decrement steps as a short delay, then returns.

name: wait_for_flag_then_store
description: Spins until bit one of a status word reached through the frame pointer is set, then stores the value two into another field of the same record.

name: wait_for_status_bit_clear
description: Calls a helper, then spins while bit five of a global control value stays set. It returns nothing.

name: wait_for_ciab_bit
description: Spins until bit four of a global variable is set, then returns. The listing shows the CIAB interrupt control register as touched.

name: prepare_track_sync_and_verify
description: Sets disk control registers and fills a buffer with eighty words of alternating-bit padding followed by the disk sync word. It then starts a transfer and checks up to six times whether the first longword read matches a fixed header pattern; on failure it records a fixed error code.

name: step_head_to_target_track
description: Steps the disk head one track at a time toward a target value, setting or clearing a direction bit and pulsing the step bit before each change while updating the stored position. It loops until the stored track equals the target.

name: forward_call_result
description: Calls one routine, saves its result, calls a second routine, and returns the saved result. It writes no memory itself.

name: call_and_pass_register
description: Calls one routine and returns the first register argument unchanged.

name: pulse_control_bits_until_clear
description: Repeatedly pulses two drive control bits and calls helpers while bit four of a global value is set. Once that bit is clear it clears a status word and returns.

name: clear_selected_control_bit
description: Clears bit seven of a global control value and calls a helper, then clears the bit selected by a frame byte's low three bits and calls another helper.

name: pulse_selected_control_bit
description: Sets bit seven and a bit selected by a frame byte's low three bits in a global control value, calls a helper, clears the selected bit, calls another helper, then sets it again.

name: interleave_word_pairs
description: Interleaves the even-numbered bits of consecutive pairs of 16-bit words into a destination buffer, with the pair count taken from a register value shifted right by one. Each output word combines the first word's even bits moved up one place with the second word's even bits.

name: call_and_return_input
description: Calls one routine and returns the value it received in its data register unchanged.

name: call_and_return_input
description: Calls one routine and returns the value it received in its data register unchanged.

name: wait_for_register_change
description: Repeats a wait a number of times taken from the argument; each wait spins on a word in a structure reached through the frame pointer. It returns nothing.

name: store_row_geometry_fields
description: Stores the first argument in two fields, clears a third, and stores the second argument in a fourth. It also computes a row-byte count as the first argument divided by eight and a product of that count with the second argument, storing both in further fields.

name: store_argument_pair_fields
description: Stores its two register arguments into two adjacent fields of a fixed record and returns nothing.

name: blit_rows_with_offsets
description: Computes row offsets and a shift from its arguments, then for each row waits for a hardware busy flag to clear and starts a transfer using the row pointers and size. The bundled listing is cut off partway, so the rest of the routine is not recoverable.

name: compute_step_count_from_bounds
description: When bit two of a flag argument is set, computes a step count from the arguments and two structure bounds and stores it in a field. When bit three is set it also stores a product in another field; the listing contains undecodable data in some paths, so those paths cannot be recovered.

name: enable_dma_after_helpers
description: Calls four helper routines, writes an enable value to a DMA-related register, then writes four control values to a global location and returns its arguments.

name: store_indexed_record_pointers
description: Looks up a word from a fixed table using the first argument, calls a helper, and stores half of two longword results into word fields of the indexed record. It then calls another helper and stores two pointer values, each offset by four bytes, into longword fields.

name: run_timer_calls_when_clear
description: Calls three routines, then when a global flag is zero calls four more before returning. The listing shows CIA timer and DMA control registers as touched through the routines it calls.
